item.title: Bayelsa boat mishap death toll rises to 32
item.description: •As Bayelsa deploys crane to lift wreckage of capsized boat •PANDEF mourns victims •Police AIG visits Ayama-Ijaw By Samuel Oyadongha & Henry Umoru The death toll in last Friday’s boat mishap in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 32, as the state government deployed a heavy-duty crane to the scene to lift the wreckage of the capsized vessel and facilitate a thorough search for persons who may still be trapped beneath or within it. This came as Pan Niger Delta Forum, PANDEF, the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone, mourned victims of the recent boat accident that claimed several lives. Also, the Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of Zone 16, Regina Udoette, has visited the Ayama-Ijaw waterside in Southern Ijaw to interact with marine workers and the Red Cross rescue team over the fatal boat mishap. The operation, involving the Bayelsa State Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, the Bayelsa State Emergency Management Agency, BYSEMA, the National Inland Waterways Authority, NIWA, security agencies, divers and other relevant responders, is continuing as the government intensifies efforts to account for all persons affected by the tragic incident. It was learned that the deployment of the crane was aimed at removing the submerged wreckage and enabling divers and rescue personnel to properly examine the site, while extending the search to areas that may not have been accessible during the initial operations. The state government had sustained the search and recovery effort since the mishap, with relevant agencies working to ensure that every part of the affected waterway and the wreckage was thoroughly examined. The latest deployment signals an escalation of the multi-agency operation, as authorities move to conclusively determine the fate of passengers who remain unaccounted for since the vessel went down. The boat tragedy, which occurred on the state’s inland waterways, around Oweikorogha and Otuan junction in the council, has once again brought to the fore concerns over water transportation safety in Bayelsa, a riverine state where boats serve as a primary means of movement for many communities. PANDEF mourns victims In a statement by PANDEF National Chairman, Amb. Godknows Igali, said: “PANDEF particularly commiserates with the affected families, the government and people of Bayelsa State, the people of Southern Ijaw council, and the affected communities, who have been impacted by this tragedy. We stand in full solidarity with them, share in their sorrow and extend the heartfelt condolences of the peoples of the entire South-South geopolitical zone. “While mourning this tragic loss, PANDEF calls on the relevant emergency relief agencies, security agencies and regulatory authorities to work closely with the Bayelsa State government to ensure that all necessary measures are taken to assuage the impact on survivors and bereaved families. “More importantly to take all necessary measur

item.title: Curfew in Delta: How gunmen killed 4 in Omo-Agege’s convoy
item.description: By Henry Umoru No fewer than four persons were killed, yesterday, as gunmen opened fire on members of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, who were on the campaign train of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, in Uduere Community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. Omo-Agege is the Delta Central Senatorial candidate of the NDC in 2027 National Assembly polls. While the NDC claimed the All Progressives Congress, APC, was responsible for the attack, the ruling party accused the NDC of stoking the attack, which, it alleged, claimed three of its members. But the state police command said it was investigating the attack. Among NDC members killed was Moses Anaughe, a former Commissioner, Federal Character Commission and aide to Omo-Agege. A former member of the Delta State House of Assembly, Chief Evans Ivwurie, was among those shot and currently battling for his life alongside other victims receiving medical attention. Videos circulating on social media showed Umukoro, popularly known as Akhima, lying motionless at a hospital where efforts were being made to revive him. Another video showed Iwurie being assisted into a hospital, with blood stains visible around his chest. This came as the Delta State government imposed a curfew on Ughelli North, following the gunshots and attendant deaths in parts of the council. Meanwhile, Ughelli North Council Chairman, Olorogun Jaro Egbo, claimed that three of his supporters were killed, with both sides accusing the each other of instigating the violence. The State Police condemned the killings, and commenced investigations to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible. The latest bloodshed was the third major violent incident linked to political activities involving rival camps in the state, following earlier clashes in the Warri-Effurun axis and Asaba, where one person was killed. While Omo-Agege’s camp put the Uduere death toll at four, Egbo claimed three of his supporters were killed, with both sides accusing each other of instigating the violence. The recurrence of deadly confrontations, with the 2027 general elections still months away, has heightened concerns over the safety of political campaigns and the possibility of Delta becoming increasingly engulfed in political violence. Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation alleged that armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage at close range during a peaceful campaign visit, describing the incident as an assassination attempt. item.title: Peter Obi lacks capacity to manage people properly — Abure
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Factional National Chairman of the Labour Party (LP), Julius Abure has accused Peter Obi of lacking the capacity to unite and manage people, citing the departure of several figures who worked with the party’s 2023 presidential candidate. Abure made the allegation on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, while explaining his fallout with Obi and his decision to support President Bola Tinubu. “Peter Obi doesn’t have capacity to manage people properly. I ask you, the structure we built around him in the 2023 general election. Where are the people? Where is Yunusa Tanko? He is in another party. You are looking at me because I’m saying I’m supporting Bola Tinubu. Yunusa Tanko is no longer with Peter,” Abure said. “Ask yourself what happened to Yunusa Tanko. Ask yourself where is Sarah Ibrahim? Where is his vice-presidential candidate in the 2023 general election? Where are a lot of others? Where is people like Valentine Ozigbo? There are many others. The man simply does not have the capacity, the character, and competence to put people together and galvanise them towards achieving a set goal.” Abure denied ever frustrating Obi out of the Labour party, saying the party had given him substantial control after the 2023 election. He argued that Obi’s experience with political parties and the Obidient movement showed, in his view, that he had struggled to keep people together. “There was no frustration, we gave him everything. We practically handed over the leadership of the party to him, and that was the truth of the matter. If you go and find out, you are journalists. I’m sure a lot of your people were with us during the campaign. “After the campaign, I practically almost handed over the party for him to run, and the result is what you have seen,” he said. “Peter Obi himself will tell you: Look at people’s past. Look at Obi’s past. Look at APGA, look at PDP, look at Labour now, and look at the people that are with him, even in the Obidient movement, how they have all abandoned him and left him because he doesn’t have that capacity to put people together and manage them for effective performance.” Abure also said his experience working with Obi, who is now contesting the 2027 election under the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), had convinced him that the former Anambra governor was “unstable” and “unreliable.” He said he chose to support Tinubu ahead of the 2027 elections because he believed the president was better suited to lead. “You see, experience they say is the best teacher. item.title: 970m Africans lack access to clean cooking — Energy expert
item.description: By Ediri Ejoh & Henry Obetta About 970 million Africans lack access to clean cooking, while over 560 million people in sub-Saharan Africa are without electricity, energy experts have said, calling for greater continental collaboration to tackle the crisis. Regional Chair for Africa of the World Energy Council, Mr Omar Farouk, disclosed this at the 14th anniversary lecture and investiture into the Realnews Hall of Fame, organised by Realnews Magazine, with the theme: “Geopolitical Turbulence and Energy Security: Forging Strategic Opportunities for Africa.” Citing the 2026 Tracking SDG 7 Report, based on 2024 data, Farouk lamented Africa’s energy poverty despite its abundant oil, gas and renewable resources. “How can a continent so richly endowed with energy resources remain so energy poor? Why do petroleum-producing countries sometimes struggle to supply affordable fuels to their own citizens? Why do countries with natural gas resources suffer from electricity shortages?” he asked. He attributed the crisis largely to inadequate finance, technology and infrastructure, rather than resource scarcity. “We cannot, as a continent, be able to get out of where we have found ourselves today if we continue to operate in silos. Our solution lies in cooperation and collaboration,” he said. Farouk stressed that finance, technology and infrastructure must work together to drive energy development, adding: “You can have a lot of money without the technology, you can’t make any progress. You can bring scientists, technologists, without the money, they can’t make progress. And you can have both of these without the energy infrastructure, you can’t move energy from one point to the other.” He said Africa was projected to attract only $110 billion, or 3.3 per cent of the estimated $3.4 trillion global energy investment in 2026, while universal clean cooking access would require about $4 billion annually. Managing Director of Frazimex Engineering Limited, a subsidiary of Oilserv Group, Engr. Chuka Eze, urged African countries to leverage global geopolitical disruptions to strengthen energy sovereignty and industrial capacity. He said Africa captures less than one per cent of the value generated from clean-energy technology manufacturing, despite its rich mineral resources. “Africa’s opportunity is to move from being a supplier of strategic resources to becoming a shaper of the global energy system,” Eze said. He called for stronger local-content policies, technology transfer, skills development and regional cooperation to promote domestic processing, manufacturing and industrial growth. item.title: Ajaokuta: NES blames collapse of long-term planning for 40-year stalemate
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The President, Nigerian Economic Society (NES), Dr. Baba Musa, has blamed the collapse of long-term economic planning for the failure of the Ajaokuta Steel Company to become operational more than four decades after its establishment. Musa, who spoke at the National Growth & Development Forum (NGDF) 2026 in Abuja, said Nigeria lost the link between economic planning and execution, resulting in the abandonment or underperformance of strategic national projects. “History demands candour. Somewhere along the way, we lost vital links between plan and performance. We built, but did not always maintain,” he said. According to him, the oil windfall of the 1970s diverted the country from agriculture and non-oil exports which had previously sustained the economy. “The oil windfall of the 1970s drew us away from the agriculture and non-oil exports that had sustained us. Strategic projects such as the Ajaokuta Steel Complex, begun with great promise, have yet to fulfil it four decades on. “And when formal planning gave way in the mid-1980s, long-term strategy too often yielded to visions that changed with administrations,” Musa said. He said Nigeria must learn from its past policy failures to avoid repeating mistakes that have undermined economic development. “The Nigeria we want must be built upon the Nigeria we have, and the Nigeria we have,” he added. The NES president also expressed concern that economic reforms had yet to translate into shared prosperity, noting that about 63 per cent of Nigerians, estimated at 140 million people, lived below the poverty line in 2025, according to the World Bank. “Macroeconomic stability is necessary, but it is not yet shared prosperity. A stable exchange rate is not yet a full dinner table. Stability is the foundation; it is not the building,” he said. Musa called for an economy that generates jobs, supports the poor, boosts domestic production, invests in human capital and promotes disciplined public finance and credible institutions. Similarly, President, Capital Market Academics of Nigeria, Prof. Uche Uwaleke, said economic reforms must be measured by their impact on citizens’ welfare, job creation, purchasing power and poverty reduction. item.title: FG seeks stronger food policies to curb malnutrition, NCDs
item.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Federal Government has called for stronger implementation of healthy food policies to address malnutrition, micronutrient deficiencies and the rising burden of diet-related non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in the country. The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr. Iziaq Adekunle Salako, made the call on Monday while delivering the keynote address at the maiden National Healthy Food Week and Learning Conference 2026 in Abuja. The conference, themed, “Our Food, Our Health, Our Future,” was organised to promote healthier food systems and strengthen efforts to address nutrition-related health challenges. Represented by the ministry’s Permanent Secretary, Ms. Daju Kachollom, Salako said tackling the country’s nutrition and health challenges required stronger collaboration among government institutions, regulatory agencies, food manufacturers, health professionals, researchers, development partners, the media and consumers. He noted that food choices and the quality of food available in markets, schools, hospitals, workplaces and homes had significant implications for public health, workforce productivity, child development and national prosperity. The minister said the Federal Government had introduced several policies and regulatory measures to improve food safety and nutritional standards, including the Revised National Policy on Food Safety and Quality and its Implementation Plan (2023). He said the policy framework promoted food safety, food fortification, sodium reduction, elimination of industrially produced trans fats and healthier food procurement practices in public institutions. Salako also highlighted the National Guidelines for Sodium Reduction, the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control’s (NAFDAC) Read the Label Campaign and the development of front-of-pack nutrition labelling as measures to help consumers make informed food choices and encourage manufacturers to improve the nutritional quality of their products. On public food procurement, he said government institutions provided millions of meals annually through schools, hospitals, correctional centres, emergency shelters and National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) camps, making public procurement an important instrument for improving the country’s food environment. He urged relevant authorities to ensure effective implementation of the Bureau of Public Procurement’s National Guidelines for Public Procurement of Food and Related Services through adequate monitoring, accountability and capacity building. The minister also identified fiscal measures, including the sugar-sweetened beverage tax, as important tools for discouraging excessive consumption of sugary drinks and generating revenue for public health interventions. He advocated transparent allocation of part of the revenue to nutrition education, healthier food environments and the prevention of diet-related diseases. item.title: 2027: NUC proposes 4-week break for universities
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The National Universities Commission NUC has proposed that universities adopt a three-to-four-week break to accommodate the 2027 general election, saying the entire election cycle will last no more than four weeks. Executive Secretary of the NUC, Prof. Abdullahi Yusufu Ribadu, made the proposal on Monday in Abuja during a courtesy visit by the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN. According to a statement from INEC on Monday night, Amupitan was accompanied by National Commissioners and senior officials of the commission. The Presidential and National Assembly elections hold on Saturday, 16 January 2027. The Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections follow on Saturday, 6 February 2027. He noted that the academic community had for over a decade served as the backbone of collation and declaration of results, with Vice-Chancellors serving as Collation and Returning Officers across the Federation. The INEC Chairman said the commission had introduced operational, technological and security reforms to make the work of its university partners safer and less contentious. He said polling unit results on Form EC8A would undergo automated arithmetic consistency and over-voting checks before transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV). According to him, the commission has procured 57,000 new Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and lowered the voter-to-device ratio to 850 per machine. Amupitan added that INEC would conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Saturday, 28 November 2026. On security, he said the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) had been decentralised to every Local Government Area and Registration Area, with dedicated security cordons and escort protocols around collation centres. He drew attention to Sections 96 and 97 of the Electoral Act 2026, which criminalise violence, abusive rhetoric and threats against electoral personnel, and Section 148, which empowers the commission to prosecute offenders directly. “No Returning Officer or Collation Officer will be left to stand alone against lawlessness,” Amupitan said. He then asked the NUC for support in four areas: the timely nomination of academic staff of verified non-partisan standing, the alignment of academic calendars with the election dates, collaboration on voter education and counter-disinformation on campuses, and the welfare and recognition of academics deployed for election duty. Responding, Ribadu congratulated Amupitan on his appointment, describing him as a lawyer and academic of international repute and “a round peg in a round hole.” , The NUC Executive Secretary said the commission would engage Vice-Chancellors on the nomination of academic staff, including through an online meeting. item.title: Trump backs Nvidia CEO’s return amid US lawmakers’ spy allegations, security concerns
item.description: US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia’s decision Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, as Democratic leaders vowed investigations and prominent Republicans questioned whether his return posed a national security risk. Trump also posted a doctored version of the famous photograph of him raising his fist after surviving a 2024 assassination attempt, replacing himself with Huang, who brandished a red bra beneath an Nvidia flag. The image appeared to allude to the scandal that forced Huang, co-founder of the AI chip giant, to resign less than two weeks earlier following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. “The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that the government had no reason to believe his return posed a national security risk. In a telephone interview with CNBC, Trump suggested the scandal could prove to be “a net positive” by highlighting Nvidia’s technological advances. “I don’t think he’s going to be diminished at all,” he said, predicting Huang would return at “an almost higher level.” He said the attorney general had confirmed that US authorities possessed no evidence Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct, but urged Nvidia to continue investigating its compliance with restrictions on advanced chip sales to China. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer and House speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries vowed sweeping investigations into Nvidia, Trump and his senior officials, with Jeffries singling out Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. “We will not allow America’s national security to be sold out by the Trump administration for personal financial gain,” Jeffries said. – ‘What changed?’ – Huang is already scheduled to face questioning behind closed doors by three House committees on December 1 over his relationship with the suspected Chinese intelligence operative and concerns about Nvidia’s chip exports. And the Republican-led Senate Banking Committee has announced that his appearance scheduled for December 3 will be livestreamed. “We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him,” said House Intelligence Committee Democrat Raja Krishnamoorthi, demanding a full public congressional hearing. Senator Elizabeth Warren called the decision “reckless” and demanded details of what input senior administration officials had provided in support of Huang’s return. Republican Senator John Curtis raised similar questions, noting that Nvidia’s board had reversed its opposition to reinstating Huang while an independent investigation remained unfinished. “Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board?” he wrote on X. “I’d like to know what changed.” Senator Pete Ricketts, also a Republican, said Huang’s behavior did not warrant reinstatement and insisted the move did not excuse him from testifying before Congress. item.title: Nigeria’s rice revolution collapses as 90 mills shutdown
item.description: *Paddy production volume crashes *From 75% self-sufficiency country goes into massive imports *Farmers abandon rice, move to other crops *Operators blame policy reversals, others *Why rice value chain now struggling —FG By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief, Jeff Agbodo (Abakiliki), Aliyu Usman (Birnin Kebbi) and Sukanmi Akanni (Lagos) Nigeria’s much-celebrated rice revolution is facing a major reversal, with more than 90 out of the country’s 260 integrated rice mills shutting down completely over acute paddy scarcity, rising production costs and the influx of cheaper imported rice. This comes as the National Rice Development Strategy II, launched in 2021 to accelerate investments and self sufficiency in rice production expires next month. The programme was part of the Buhari administration’s agricultural transformation agenda, which sought to reduce dependence on food imports and conserve foreign exchange. Nigeria had announced 75 per cent self-sufficiency in rice production in February 2023 and projected to become a net exporter of the commodity by 2026. The progress was showcased in January 2023 when the Federal Government, the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, and Rice Farmers Association of Nigeria, RIFAN, unveiled what they described as the world’s largest rice pyramids in Abuja. The pyramids, comprising one million bags of paddy, were presented as evidence of Nigeria’s growing capacity to produce enough rice for domestic consumption and eventually export the commodity. Nigeria’s annual rice import bill, estimated at about $1 billion in 2015, was said to have fallen to approximately $18.5 million by 2021. But the year 2025 marked the beginning of the reversal of fortune with Paddy production, which had risen to 8.5 million tonnes in 2021, recording a sharp decline to about 4.8 million tonnes, while mill capacity utilisation dropped below 30 per cent. Industry operators told Financial Vanguard that leading integrated mills, including Umza in Kano and Stallion in Lagos, are operating below 50 per cent of their installed capacity. Speaking to the unfolding crisis the National Chairman of the Rice Millers Association of Nigeria, RIMAN, and Chairman, Board of Trustees of the Competitive African Rice Forum for Sustainable Development, CARF-FSD, Nigeria Chapter, Mr. Peter Dama, noted the rice policy inconsistency especially the suspension of the Anchor Borrowers’ Programme (ABP), which drove the country’s rice production surge between 2015 and 2023. The industry operators listed inadequate agricultural financing, insecurity, escalating input costs and weak supply chains as key in the derailing of the growth over the past three years. More recently they said that 2026 has witnessed a deliberate opening of the country’s borders allowing massive importation of cheaper foreign rice especially through Seme border with Benin Republic. item.title: 2027: ‘As You Do For Me, I Do For You,’ Tinubu Seeks Igbo Support In Lagos
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has appealed to Igbo residents in Lagos State to support his re-election bid in the 2027 general elections. President Tinubu made the call while addressing Igbo stakeholders at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, Iganmu, Lagos, on Monday. ﻿ President Tinubu said that though he was displeased when he lost the 2023 election in the state, which is considered a stronghold of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), the matter had been settled. “Some of you didn’t vote for me in 2023; I vex o . We don settle. Get your PVC,” he urged the crowd. Tinubu also asked if they would vote for him, to which they replied with a resounding “Yes.” After receiving assurance from the stakeholders to back his re-election bid, the president said, “Come January 16, get your PVC; you come vote. Agreement na agreement o, na Bola Tinubu be APC o. As you do for me, I do for you.” ‘Follow Who Know Road’ President Tinubu called for national unity and collective responsibility, urging Nigerians to see themselves as one people with a shared future, in the interest of the country. “You must follow who know road. I have to work hard to make sure the economy improves, to ensure that your children are in school, to eliminate crises in the universities, to build good roads that will maintain our cars. “The future is in our hands. For every one of us, our children must be in school. Because we are poor doesn’t mean they shouldn’t attend the universities,” he added. Tinubu further said the country must rise above its divisions, noting that its development depended on the participation and commitment of all its people. Also speaking, the Governor of Lagos State, Mr Babajide Sanwo-Olu, urged Igbo residents to support Tinubu’s re-election and vote for all candidates of the APC in the 2027 general elections. The governor also implored them to work for the emergence of the Deputy Governor and APC governorship candidate, Obafemi Hamzat, as the next Governor of Lagos State. During the meeting, the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi; the Minister of State for Budget and Planning, Doris Uzoka-Anite; and the former Minister of Labour and Employment, Nkiruka Onyejeocha, as well as other Igbo leaders and stakeholders, assured President Tinubu of their support. The Independent National Electoral Commission said Peter Obi, who was the candidate of the Labour Party, polled 582,454 votes in Lagos, higher than the 572,606 votes polled by Tinubu in the February 25, 2023 presidential election. Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial hub, has one of the highest numbers of registered voters for the 2027 general elections. Emphasising the electoral importance of Lagos, Tinubu described it as a big deal to him. ”To me, Lagos is the big deal. item.title: Gov. Mutfwang loses brother
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa Plateau State Governor, Caleb Manasseh Mutfwang, has lost his elder brother, Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang, who died Sunday night following a protracted illness, family sources have disclosed. The Plateau State Government confirmed the death on Monday, as the State Executive Council and the Plateau State Inter-Religious Council paid separate condolence visits to the Governor’s family at the Government House, Jos. The Deputy Governor, Ngo Josephine Piyo, who led members of the State Executive Council on a condolence visit to the Governor’s Residence at the Old Government House, Jos, described the deceased as “a distinguished personality, a devoted family man, a lover of peace and a patriotic Nigerian who made meaningful contributions to public service.” She said the Council received the news of his passing “with profound shock and sadness,” noting that his death was “not only a painful loss to the Mutfwang family but also a significant loss to Plateau State and the nation, given his contributions to society and his exemplary life.” Piyo prayed for the peaceful repose of his soul and asked Almighty God to grant the Governor, the bereaved family and all those mourning his demise “the strength, grace and fortitude to bear the tragic loss.” In a separate visit, the Plateau State Inter-Religious Council also condoled with the Governor and his family over the death of Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang. The delegation, led by the Emir of Wase, Alhaji (Dr.) Muhammadu Sambo Haruna, who spoke on behalf of the Council’s Co-Chairman, Rev. Prof. Pandam Yamsat, described the deceased’s passing as “a painful loss to the family and the state.” Haruna acknowledged the inevitability of death as part of the human experience, urging the bereaved family to “find solace in the sovereignty and wisdom of Almighty God.” He also prayed that God would grant the family “the comfort, strength and resilience needed to navigate this difficult period.” Responding on behalf of the family during the separate condolence visits, Mr. Jonathan Mutfwang expressed “profound appreciation to both delegations for their thoughtful gesture, solidarity and prayers.” He noted that their presence had brought “considerable comfort and encouragement to the bereaved family at this difficult time.” Jonathan also prayed for God’s continued protection, blessings and preservation upon members of the delegations. The family disclosed that the burial of the late Arc. Morris Manasseh Mutfwang has been scheduled for Thursday, November 26, 2026. The condolence visits were disclosed in a statement signed by the Director of Press and Public Affairs to the Governor, Gyang Bere, PhD, and made available to newsmen in Jos on Monday. The post Gov. item.title: Delta govt imposes curfew in Ughelli North after campaign rally violence
item.description: The Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew in Ughelli North Local Government Area following reported violence at a campaign rally of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Uduere Community, which allegedly left some people dead and several others injured. The curfew, which takes effect from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily, will remain in force until further notice. The Delta State Police Command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bright Edafe. According to the statement, the police have commenced investigations to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and identify those responsible. The Command urged residents to comply strictly with the curfew and cooperate with security personnel to maintain peace and public safety. The statement reads, “The Command therefore urges residents of Ughelli North Local Government Area to comply strictly with the curfew imposed by the Delta State Government, restricting movement between 1800hrs to 0600hrs until further notice. Residents are advised to remain calm and cooperate with security personnel in the interest of public safety. “The Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, CP Samuel E. Erale, psc, mnips, has directed intensified security operations in the affected area to prevent further violence and maintain law and order. The CP has ordered a full-scale investigation and assures residents of the state that anyone found culpable will face the full weight of the law, irrespective of political affiliation or status, and urges members of the public to provide credible information to assist ongoing investigations.” Erale also extended his condolences to the families of those who died and wished the injured a speedy recovery. He reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to protecting lives and property while ensuring a peaceful environment for lawful political activities. The police commissioner further warned political actors and their supporters against thuggery, intimidation and the unlawful use of firearms. He stressed that political differences must never be allowed to degenerate into violence or loss of lives. item.title: 89 fall ill after unknown substance released at UK Arena concert
item.description: Thousands of concertgoers were evacuated from the UK’s largest indoor arena after the release of an “unknown substance”, with dozens reporting suffering side effects, police said Monday. Some 12,000 people were attending the Sunday night show by US rapper Don Toliver at the Co-op Live arena in Manchester, northwest England. “A total of 89 people displayed symptoms believed to be linked to exposure,” Manchester police said, adding one woman was taken to hospital for treatment. “Enquiries remain ongoing to establish the nature of the substance, where it came from and any associated risk,” Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said in a statement. Toliver said he had postponed his Monday night London show following the incident, which led to one person being taken to hospital. Emergency services were called after “reports of people in the crowd suffering effects from an unknown substance”, Manchester police said, declaring a major incident at the scene. The venue, which bills itself as the country’s largest live entertainment arena, said it was working with police to “identify the cause of the incident”. The regional ambulance service said it assessed more than 50 people, including some reporting “eye and respiratory symptoms”. Toliver, who was nominated for five Grammy Awards last week, is currently on the second leg of his “Nitrous” world tour. He announced he was rescheduling his show at London’s O2 arena due to an “unfortunate incident last night (in) Manchester”. “My heart and prayers are with everyone that was injured last night,” Toliver said on Instagram, without providing more details. Concertgoers told the BBC that people were “choking” and coughing, recalling “distressing scenes” of people leaving the venue in a panic. Some criticised the lack of security checks at the venue, especially in a city still scarred by the 2017 Manchester Arena bombing, which killed 22 people at an Ariana Grande concert. item.title: 2027: Armed Men Who Killed Four NDC Campaign Members Said I Was Their Target, Omo-Agege
item.description: Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has alleged that the gunmen who attacked his campaign team in Delta State, killing four people, repeatedly shouted his name and declared their intention to kill him. Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central Senatorial District on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 general elections, said he escaped the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services (DSS) escorts. He spoke on Monday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today . ﻿ Recounting the incident, the former deputy senate president said he heard the attackers repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him while opening fire at the campaign venue. “Right there at the venue, while they were shooting, we could hear them say, ‘It is Omo-Agege we want to kill. We must kill Omo-Agege.’ “But I was lucky because my DSS details were very professional. In fact, after God, the only reason I am alive today is because of the DSS operatives who were with me,” he said. Omo-Agege described the incident as a premeditated attack, alleging that there had been a build-up to the violence. He questioned why he would be singled out for elimination when several other politicians were also contesting elective positions. The former lawmaker said the attackers struck less than five minutes after he began addressing supporters at the campaign venue. According to him, he had moved towards the side of his vehicle to make eye contact with members of the audience when the gunshots rang out. “It was by divine intervention. As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of the vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started,” he said. The former deputy senate president said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others sustained injuries, with some in critical condition. ﻿ In a statement issued earlier on Monday by his media adviser, Sunny Areh, Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation said he survived an assassination attempt during a campaign tour in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. Areh alleged that armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage while he was addressing supporters during a campaign visit. The organisation called for an independent and thorough investigation by the Nigeria Police Force, while appealing to the Inspector-General of Police, the DSS, INEC, civil society organisations and the international community to ensure the safety of political candidates and their supporters. It also urged supporters to remain calm and avoid retaliation, adding that its ward-to-ward campaign activities across Delta Central would continue. item.title: Obi Meets Niger State Residents, Urges Nigerians To Turn Out For 2027 Elections
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians to turn out en masse for the 2027 general elections and remain at their polling units until their votes are counted and transmitted. Obi made the call during a campaign visit to Suleja, Niger State, where he urged voters to resist attempts to manipulate the outcome of the elections by ensuring that their votes were properly accounted for. He also criticised President Bola Tinubu, claiming that the president lacked the physical strength required to govern the country and was more interested in retaining power for personal gains than serving Nigerians. Obi, who is seeking the presidency for the second time, also promised to address Nigeria’s electricity challenges, pledging that his administration would generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000 megawatts of electricity if elected. Niger residents gather for an engagement of NDC Presidential candidate Peter Obi. Photo: NigeriaNDCHQ/X He said Niger State would play a role in achieving the target, citing the state’s resources as part of the potential support for his proposed power-sector plan. The former Anambra State governor has been holding town hall meetings and engaging residents in different states ahead of the 2027 general elections. NDC Presidential candidate Peter Obi. Photo: NigeriaNDCHQ/X Obi contested the 2023 presidential election under the Labour Party, finishing third with 6,101,533 votes, behind Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, who polled 8,794,726 votes, and Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, who received 6,984,520 votes. Tinubu is seeking re-election in 2027, while Obi is contesting under the NDC. Ahead of the election, major contenders include Tinubu under the APC, Atiku of the ADC, and Obi of the NDC. Other parties include the AAC, PDP, APM, SDP, PRP, Labour Party, and YPP. The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections are slated for February 6, 2027.
